intro: I am an undergraduate in Computer Science at Communication University of China. I learn machine learning by building small systems, reproducing experiments, and carefully studying where they fail.
researchStatement: My current interest is multimodal machine learning, especially how visual information is compressed, aligned, and evaluated in language-model pipelines. I am early in my research training and am looking for an environment where I can learn rigorous methods while contributing careful engineering, reproducible experiments, and honest analysis of negative results.

project.title: DeepSeek-OCR Reproduction
project.summary: Built a lightweight DeepSeek-OCR-style pipeline on an 8GB laptop GPU, then designed diagnostics to explain why the trained model learned document-style priors instead of reading the page.
highlights: Constructed a 428M SigLIP encoder, convolutional visual compressor, projection layer, and Qwen2.5 decoder pipeline with two-stage LoRA training.
Trained on 5,393 olmOCR pages and evaluated against OmniDocBench without using the benchmark in training.
Found that both 256-token and 1024-token visual budgets produced page-level template collapse, pointing to the frozen encoder and loss of temporal character alignment rather than token count alone.
Compared Qwen2.5-0.5B and 1.5B, soft CTC OCR tokens, hybrid text-plus-soft-token inputs, and formula oversampling on rented GPUs.
